transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Oh, hello Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time with this... but, well, for the past year or so, I just feel like I’m always... puttering around. You know, fixing little things, arranging the house, or volunteering for just one more committee or church thing. 

Which is a good thing, right? Keeping busy is supposed to be good for you! But... I suppose the reason I'm here is that, even at 87, I just have such a hard time just sitting down and being still. I always have to be doing *something*, and I guess it's gotten a little out of hand. I hope that's an okay reason to come see you? Does that make sense?
During this past year, have you found yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different everyday things?

Oh, goodness, no, I don't think so. I mean... I hope I don't sound like a worrywart! I really do try my best to look on the bright side of things. 

It's more just that I... well, I just like to keep my hands busy, you know? But as for actually sitting and fretting about everyday things... no, I haven't really noticed that. I'm sorry if that's not what you were looking for, but I hope that answers your question alright?
During this past year, have you noticed a change in your sleep, such as needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling fully energized?

Oh, my, no. I definitely still need my rest! I mean... at my age, a good night's sleep is quite important, you know? 

I haven't noticed needing less sleep at all. When it's bedtime, I'm certainly ready to close my eyes, and if I happen to not get enough sleep, I definitely feel tired the next day. I'm certainly not running around feeling fully energized without any sleep, goodness no. It's just that when I *am* awake during the day, I just like to be up and doing things. 

I hope that's normal? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly, Doctor.
When you are arranging things or fixing things around the house, do you feel uncomfortable or anxious if they aren't done in a very specific, exact way?

Oh, goodness, no, I wouldn't say that. I really try not to be a fussy person! I mean... I like a tidy house, naturally, but it certainly doesn't have to be just perfectly exact. 

If something is a little out of place, or if I do a chore a little differently one day, it doesn't bother me or make me anxious at all. It's really more about just... the act of doing it, I suppose? Just keeping moving. I don't need things to be a certain way, I just need to be doing *something*. 

I hope that's helpful? I know you're trying to figure all this out, and I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Did you have similar trouble sitting still or feeling restless when you were a child?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose I did, yes. I hope you won't think terribly of me, but... I do remember back in grade school, oh, long before I was even a teenager, I used to get scolded just a little bit. 

I had this silly habit of just... popping right out of my seat when I wasn't supposed to. And, well, I might have talked over my classmates from time to time. The teachers always just said I was 'too lively.' I really didn't mean to be disruptive, Doctor, I just had so much spirit and always wanted to be involved in whatever was happening! 

I hope I don't sound like I was a naughty child. I always did try my very best to be good and polite. Is that the sort of thing you were wondering about? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right details.
